summary:
TrendLens Lite is an interactive web application that helps users explore long-term temperature and precipitation patterns across cities in Bangladesh using NASA POWER data. Users can select a city, choose an environmental variable, and examine annual trends through interactive visualizations and statistical analysis.

The project uses NASA POWER monthly point data to make Earth system information more accessible and understandable. By presenting climate data through a simple interface, TrendLens Lite helps students, researchers, and the public explore environmental changes and develop a better understanding of local climate patterns.

Our goal is to make climate data exploration more approachable, informative, and accessible.
details:
TrendLens Lite is a web-based climate data exploration tool developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 challenge, “Be An Earth System Trend Detective!”

The application allows users to explore temperature and precipitation patterns across selected cities in Bangladesh using NASA POWER monthly point data. It uses the MERRA-2 data source and the parameters T2M (air temperature at 2 meters) and PRECTOTCORR (corrected precipitation).

Users can select a city and environmental variable, view annual summaries through interactive graphs, and examine long-term trends using statistical methods. The application includes Theil–Sen slope estimation and Kendall trend analysis, helping users investigate the direction and strength of possible trends. Users can also export data as CSV files for further exploration.

TrendLens Lite was designed to make climate information easier to explore without requiring users to work directly with raw datasets or programming tools. Its simple interface makes it useful for students, educators, researchers, and anyone interested in understanding local climate patterns.

The application was developed using Python, Streamlit, Pandas, Plotly, and statistical analysis tools. The project combines NASA Earth science data with accessible data visualization and interactive analysis.

The project focuses on making climate data more approachable while encouraging informed exploration of environmental trends. Its results should be interpreted as gridded, reanalysis-informed estimates rather than direct measurements from individual weather stations.
